The CARD11 E626K mutation resides in the linker domain of the protein and has been identified in patients with Sezary Syndrome. Expression of the E626K mutation in Jurkat T cells constitutively activates NF-κB and TCR signalling in a gain-of-function manner. In addition, the alteration causes enhanced JNK phosphorylation (PMID: 26551667).
There is suggestive but not definitive evidence for gain-of-function behaviour, and the mechanism remains incompletely resolved.

Truncating mutations in DTX1 generally occur in the exon 1 WWE1 domain of the protein. These mutations have been identified in patients with diffuse large B-Cell Lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphomas (PMID: 25171927). In vitro studies with mammalian cells expressing a truncated DTX1 mutant lacking domain III demonstrated that truncation mutations are likely inactivating as measured by the inability to inhibit MASH1-mediated transcriptional activation compared to full transcript DTX1 (PMID: 11564735).
